description: The OUTER squeeze loop that drives the framac-sl base loop across a whole C/C++ codebase (sl-monitoring-sl: a squeeze loop monitoring a squeeze loop). It runs a Phase-0 architectural audit, builds the unit dependency graph, schedules units leaf-first, and instantiates a framac-sl sub-loop per unit. Its lower bound is the base loop's own machine WP verdicts (a differential comparator), its upper bound the mission guidance + a framac-gold reference. The dominant coherent-and-wrong it guards: a codebase that looks 'verified' because every sub-loop reported green, yet hides a faithful-but-incomplete spec, a smuggled behavioural axiom, a vacuous green, a gold-coverage gap, or an unsound Coq escalation — failures a single-gate monitor cannot see, which is why the base-SL monitor runs FOUR gates per unit plus a Coq-soundness audit.

disjointness.rationale: The outer loop never certifies the base loop's deliverable with the same pair that produced it: the coordinator holds the mission guidance and judges only the aggregated machine verdicts; the architect reads the source read-only against the documented intent but verifies nothing; the scheduler reads the compile graph against the audit ranking but proves nothing; the base-SL monitor squeezes the base loop's machine verdicts + a cache-clean Coq replay (L) against the mission guidance + a cross-provider framac-gold (U) over four distinct gates, and is physically barriered from the base agents' private rationale (it is a differential comparator over verdicts, not a reader of reasoning). The framac-sl instances are the bridge row: the whole base cast collapsed to one line, reading the per-unit requirement against the per-unit WP gates — its real disjointness lives in framac-sl's own document. The base-SL monitor's L and the bridge row's L are deliberately DISTINCT: the bridge reads the per-unit WP gates while the monitor reads the AGGREGATED verdicts plus the cache-clean Coq replay as a differential comparator.
disjointness.load_bearing_barrier: base-SL monitor ⊥ base rationale — the monitor judges the base loop only through its machine WP verdicts and a re-run Coq oracle, never the producers' reasoning. Reading base rationale would collapse the monitor into the loop it monitors. Inherited base barriers are never weakened: driving framac-sl as a sub-loop adds barriers, it never removes the base's.

catchability.blind_spot: mis-scopes / silently drops an attack-surface module; asserts a claim not in the code
catchability.via: the gold-completeness gate squeezes per-unit coverage against framac-gold and surfaces a dropped/mis-scoped unit

catchability.blind_spot: emits a unit with wrong preprocessing flags / a non-parsing or mis-ordered unit
catchability.via: the base sub-loop fails to parse/discharge the unit, exposing the bad flags or order

catchability.blind_spot: a faithful-but-incomplete spec, a smuggled behavioural axiom, a vacuous green, or an unsound Coq escalation reported as green
catchability.via: the four gates (faithfulness / Gate B / non-vacuity / gold-completeness) + the cache-clean Coq replay + Print Assumptions audit

catchability.blind_spot: the monitor itself rubber-stamps a gate or runs gold within one model family (the owed decorrelation)
catchability.via: the coordinator adjudicates the verdict log and refuses 'done' on a sub-loop's say-so, routing the decorrelation gap to getting-better/

catchability.blind_spot: bad framing / accepts the codebase done on aggregate green without cross-unit discharge
catchability.via: the per-unit four-gate verdicts withhold green from any un-gated unit, so the coordinator cannot aggregate to done
